thread:
michaela: Quick sync — followup to the delegation RFC. We need to pick heuristics for delegation expiry + how telemetry should attribute delegated calls. Two main questions: 1) default TTL and max TTL for delegated API keys/tokens, and 2) should usage/billing/telemetry be attributed to the original actor or the operator service?

jordan: +1. We also need to decide refresh behavior (lazy refresh vs proactive) and whether we enforce jitter to avoid thundering refreshes.

lee: Proposal from my side: default TTL 15m, max TTL 1h, refresh lazy (on first use when <30s left) with exponential backoff for retries. Add uniform jitter +-10%. Reason: keeps key lifetimes short but avoids frequent rotation storms.

nora: Curious about the attribution model. If we attribute to the original actor, dashboards will show accurate user behavior but billing/quotas become tricky (operator may not want per-customer billing spikes). If we attribute to operator, we lose visibility into end-user flows. Tradeoffs.

sam: Ops perspective: attributing billing to operator service makes quota enforcement easier (single quota bucket), and fallback policies are simpler. But we should at least surface original_actor_id in telemetry so we can slice traces.

michaela: Agreed. Can we emit telemetry with two explicit fields: attributed_actor (who gets billed/quota) and origin_actor (the original principal)? That keeps billing simple but preserves visibility. Thoughts? :thinking:

lee: That works. Implementation sketch: token metadata carries {attributed_actor, origin_actor, delegation_chain}. Runtime logging emits both. We also need to ensure origin_actor is sampled in high-volume paths to avoid egress costs.

jordan: On sampling: default to 1% sampling for origin_actor in high-throughput endpoints, 100% for admin routes. Make it configurable per-route.

nora: Back to TTLs — some services have long-running jobs and will complain about 15m. Can we support per-service overrides and a negotiation at mint time? e.g., client requests desired_ttl up to max_ttl, operator policy approves.

sam: Yes, per-service allowed. Suggest policy evaluation at mint: service_policy.allowed_max_ttl and requested_ttl -> granted_ttl = min(requested, allowed_max). Audit event emitted.

michaela: Good. Need an API surface for that. Rough sketch:
```
POST /v1/delegate
body: { "actor": "svc-A", "target_service": "svc-B", "requested_ttl": 3600 }
response: { "token": "ey...", "granted_ttl": 1800, "attributed_actor": "svc-A", "origin_actor": "user:123" }
```

lee: Also include a header/field for refresh_deadline so clients can schedule refreshes without parsing token expiry. e.g., "refresh_after": 1350 (seconds) when granted_ttl 1500.

jordan: Security note: ensure redeemed tokens carry proof of delegation (signed blob) so downstream services can verify delegation chain without contacting issuer on every request. But keep blob size small. Maybe compress and base64.

sec-bot: Reminder: per policy, max delegation chain length = 3. Logs will flag chains > allowed during issuance. (automated check) :robot_face:

nora: Good catch. Also need to document revocation semantics — immediate revoke should invalidate outstanding delegated tokens ASAP. We need a revocation stream/notification to edge proxies.

sam: We already have a lightweight revocation pubsub used for API key invalidation. Can extend it for delegated tokens; proxies subscribe and drop tokens when revoked. Propagation time measured ~2s in env-staging.

michaela: Perf question: how does telemetry attribution affect metrics cardinality? origin_actor will explode cardinality. We must avoid adding origin_actor to core metrics; instead keep it as a tag only in traces/logs and as a sampled dimension for metrics.

lee: Agree. Implementation rule: core metrics use attributed_actor only. origin_actor appears in logs/traces and in sampled metrics pipelines (1% default).

jordan: One more tradeoff: should delegated tokens be exchangeable for longer-lived tokens in downstream services for background work? That leaks the original actor's intent. I'd bias to disallow any extension unless explicitly approved by policy.

nora: Policy-based elevate-flow sounds right: operator can request escalation via multi-party approval (e.g., owner consent). Otherwise deny.

michaela: OK action items: 1) formalize default policy: default_ttl=900, max_ttl=3600, jitter +-10%, lazy refresh at 30s threshold, chain_length<=3, sampled origin_actor 1% by default. 2) API sketch for /delegate + refresh_after field. 3) telemetry contract: attributed_actor for billing/metrics, origin_actor only in logs/traces and sampled metrics. 4) revocation via existing pubsub.

sam: I'll own the revocation extension and proxy subscription.

lee: I'll draft the config schema + code example and a short RFC appendix for signed delegation blobs.

jordan: I'll draft the telemetry contract and sampling defaults for product/marketing.

nora: I'll write the policy wording for per-service allowed_max_ttl and escalation flow.

michaela: Great — let's reconvene after PRs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
